# `silk/text/bidi`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

The Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm (UAX #9) for text that mixes left-to-right and right-to-left
scripts, with data from Unicode 18.0.0.

## When to use
Use [`BidiAnalysis`](#BidiAnalysis) to find the direction and embedding level of each part of a text that can
contain Arabic, Hebrew or other right-to-left scripts. Use [`reorder`](#reorder) to put the parts of a
wrapped line in visual order.

## Details
[`BidiAnalysis.analyze`](#BidiAnalysis.impl.analyze) implements the whole algorithm of UAX #9 revision 52: explicit
embeddings, overrides and isolates, overflow handling, bracket pairs (N0), and the removal of
formatting characters (X9). Its results are paragraphs and level runs over the byte offsets of
the text. Paragraphs without right-to-left characters, Arabic digits or explicit formatting
take a fast path. [`analyzeClasses`](#analyzeClasses) and [`analyzeCodepoints`](#analyzeCodepoints) resolve one paragraph of classes
or code points, for conformance tests.

## Gotchas
The analysis applies rule L1 only with each paragraph as one line, in
[`BidiRun.unwrappedLevel`](#BidiRun.unwrappedLevel). After you wrap a paragraph, apply rule L1 to each line yourself
before [`reorder`](#reorder).

## Examples
### Find the right-to-left part of a text
```silk
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.text.bidi { BidiAnalysis, ParagraphDirection }

pub effect fn main() -> i32
  ! OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let mut analysis = BidiAnalysis.make()
  // "abc " followed by the Hebrew letters alef, bet and gimel.
  run analysis.analyze("abc \u{5d0}\u{5d1}\u{5d2}", ParagraphDirection.Auto)
    |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  let runs = analysis.runs()
  // The Hebrew run starts at byte 4 and has the right-to-left level 1.
  if runs.length != 2 || runs[1].start != 4 || runs[1].level != 1 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `bidi` with `import silk.text.bidi as bidi`.

The base direction of the paragraphs of a text.

<a id="ParagraphDirection.Auto"></a>

### `Auto`

```silk
Auto
```

Each paragraph takes the direction of its first strong character (rules P2 and P3), and is
left-to-right when it has none.

<a id="BidiParagraph"></a>

## `BidiParagraph`

```silk
pub struct BidiParagraph
```

One paragraph of a text, as [`BidiAnalysis.paragraphs`](#BidiAnalysis.impl.paragraphs) gives it.

### Details

A paragraph ends after each paragraph separator, such as LF or U+2029 (rule P1). CR and LF each
end a paragraph, so CRLF gives an empty paragraph between them.

<a id="BidiParagraph.start"></a>

### Field `start`

```silk
pub start: usize
```

The byte offset where the paragraph starts.

<a id="BidiParagraph.end"></a>

### Field `end`

```silk
pub end: usize
```

The byte offset where the paragraph ends, after its paragraph separator.

<a id="BidiParagraph.level"></a>

### Field `level`

```silk
pub level: u8
```

The paragraph embedding level: 0 for left-to-right, 1 for right-to-left.

<a id="BidiParagraph.hasStrong"></a>

### Field `hasStrong`

```silk
pub hasStrong: bool
```

True if the paragraph has a strong character outside isolates (rule P2). An
[`ParagraphDirection.Auto`](#ParagraphDirection.Auto) paragraph without one is left-to-right.

<a id="BidiWorkspace"></a>

## `BidiWorkspace`

```silk
pub struct BidiWorkspace
```

The per-character results of one paragraph, as [`analyzeClasses`](#analyzeClasses) and [`analyzeCodepoints`](#analyzeCodepoints)
give them.

### When to use

Use a `BidiWorkspace` to resolve one paragraph of bidi classes or code points and read the level
of each character, as the Unicode conformance tests do. Use [`BidiAnalysis`](#BidiAnalysis) for text.

### Details

The workspace keeps its storage across calls. Each analysis replaces its contents. Character
`index` is the position in the input of the analysis.

<a id="BidiAnalysis"></a>

## `BidiAnalysis`

```silk
pub struct BidiAnalysis
```

The results of the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm (UAX #9) for one text: its paragraphs and its
level runs.

### When to use

Use a `BidiAnalysis` to lay out text that can mix left-to-right and right-to-left scripts, such
as English with Arabic or Hebrew. Shape each [`BidiRun`](#BidiRun) in its direction, then order the runs
of each line with [`reorder`](#reorder).

### Details

[`BidiAnalysis.analyze`](#BidiAnalysis.impl.analyze) fills the analysis. It implements the whole algorithm: explicit
embeddings, overrides and isolates, bracket pairs, and the removal of formatting characters
(X9). The runs cover the text in logical order. An analysis keeps its storage, so reuse one
analysis for many texts.

<a id="BidiAnalysis.impl.analyze"></a>

### Method `analyze`

```silk
pub effect fn analyze(self: &mut Self, text: string, direction: ParagraphDirection) -> ()
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Replaces the results with those for `text`, with `direction` as the base direction of each
paragraph.

#### Details

A paragraph ends after each paragraph separator; CR and LF each count (rule P1). With
[`ParagraphDirection.Auto`](#ParagraphDirection.Auto), each paragraph takes its own direction (rules P2 and P3).
Offsets in the results are byte offsets into `text`. The analysis keeps its storage, so a
later call allocates only when a text needs more.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot grow the storage of the analysis.

<a id="analyzeClasses"></a>

## `analyzeClasses`

```silk
pub effect fn analyzeClasses(
  classes: &[BidiClass],
  direction: ParagraphDirection,
  workspace: &mut BidiWorkspace,
) -> u8
  ! OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Allocator
```

Resolves one paragraph of bidi classes into `workspace`, and returns the paragraph embedding
level.

### When to use

Use `analyzeClasses` to test the algorithm against class sequences, as the Unicode `BidiTest.txt`
file gives them. Use [`BidiAnalysis.analyze`](#BidiAnalysis.impl.analyze) for text.

### Details

The input is one paragraph: a paragraph separator class does not start a new one. Classes have
no bracket identity, so no bracket pairs are found.

### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot grow `workspace`.

### When to use

Use `analyzeCodepoints` to test the algorithm against code point sequences, as the Unicode
`BidiCharacterTest.txt` file gives them. Use [`BidiAnalysis.analyze`](#BidiAnalysis.impl.analyze) for text.

### Details

The input is one paragraph: a paragraph separator does not start a new one. Bracket pairs use
the Unicode paired-bracket properties.

### Errors

<a id="reorder"></a>

## `reorder`

```silk
pub effect fn reorder(levels: &[u8], output: &mut List<usize>) -> ()
  ! OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Allocator
```

Appends the indices of `levels` to `output` in visual order (rule L2).

### When to use

Use `reorder` for each line after wrapping: take the levels of the characters or runs of the
line, apply rule L1 to them, and reorder.

### Details

`levels` holds the embedding level of each item of one line, in logical order, after rule L1.
Leave out the characters that rule X9 removes. The function reverses each maximal sequence at
or above each odd level, from the highest level down. It does not allocate scratch storage.

### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot grow `output`.
